title: Refine the backlog
summary: Refinement is a regular session where the team makes upcoming backlog items clear, small and ready to build. It makes sprint planning quick and calm.

beginner: Hold a short session once or twice a sprint.
Bring the top items in priority order.
For each, explain the user need and ask the team questions.
Agree acceptance criteria and split items that are too big.
Ask the team to estimate the size.
Aim to have about two sprints of ready work.
intermediate: Run regular refinement with clear entry and exit criteria.
Split large items by user value.
Keep about two sprints of ready work.
experienced: Involve design and engineering early so items arrive well shaped.
Use refinement to surface risk and dependencies.
Keep refinement light and avoid over-specifying.

toolExamples.jira: Use a 'ready' status or label so the team can see what is ready for planning.
toolExamples.azure-devops: Use the backlog view with a 'ready' tag.
toolExamples.linear: Use a triage and backlog state for unrefined and ready work.

definitionOfDone: Top items have clear acceptance criteria
Items small enough for a sprint
About two sprints of ready work
pitfalls: PM presenting with no team questions
Skipping refinement and doing it in planning
